test_title: PYST 70: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held On 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Read the below statements about synaptic transmission:

1. Synaptic cleft is the gap between two neurons.

2. Neurotransmitters are released from presynaptic terminals.

3. Axon hillock receives impulses from the next neuron.

Which of the above statements are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Synaptic cleft is the gap between two neurons.

 
 
• The **synaptic cleft** is a small gap (usually around 20-40 nanometers wide) that exists between the **presynaptic neuron** and the **postsynaptic neuron**.
 
• This gap allows for the transmission of chemical signals (neurotransmitters) from one neuron to another.
 
• *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** Neurotransmitters are released from presynaptic terminals.
 
 
• Neurotransmitters are chemical messengers that are stored in vesicles located in the **axon terminals of the presynaptic neuron**.
 
• When an action potential reaches the presynaptic terminal, these neurotransmitters are released into the synaptic cleft via a process called **exocytosis**.
 
• The neurotransmitters then bind to specific receptors on the postsynaptic neuron, leading to signal transmission.
 
• *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:** Axon hillock receives impulses from the next neuron.
 
 
• The **axon hillock** is the region of the neuron where the axon emerges from the cell body (soma). It is responsible for generating action potentials.
 
• However, it does not receive impulses from the next neuron. Instead, it integrates signals received by the dendrites and soma of the neuron.
 
• Signals from the **next neuron** are received by the **dendrites** or cell body via synapses.
 
• *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Synapse:**

 
 
• A synapse is a junction between two neurons or between a neuron and a target cell (such as a muscle cell). It facilitates the transfer of signals.
 
• There are two types of synapses: **chemical synapses** (which involve neurotransmitters) and **electrical synapses** (which involve direct electrical communication).
 
 
 
• **Neurotransmitters:**
 
 
• These are chemical substances that transmit signals across the synaptic cleft. Examples include **acetylcholine**, **dopamine**, **serotonin**, and **glutamate**.
 
• Neurotransmitters can be excitatory (e.g., glutamate) or inhibitory (e.g., GABA).
 
 
 
• **Axon Hillock and Action Potential:**
 
 
• The axon hillock is the decision-making point of the neuron where the summation of excitatory and inhibitory signals determines whether an action potential will be generated.
 
• It is rich in voltage-gated sodium channels, which are essential for initiating the action potential.
 
 
 
• **Signal Transmission:**
 
 
• Neuronal communication involves the conversion of electrical signals into chemical signals and then back into electrical signals.
 
• This process ensures accurate and efficient signal relay across neurons in the nervous system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The synaptic cleft ensures that signals are unidirectional, moving from the presynaptic neuron to the postsynaptic neuron.
 
• Neurotransmitters are stored in synaptic vesicles and released upon the arrival of an action potential.
 
• The postsynaptic neuron has specific receptors that determine the effect of the neurotransmitter (excitation or inhibition).
 
• Understanding synaptic transmission is crucial for studying brain functions, including learning, memory, and diseases like Parkinson’s or Alzheimer’s.
